# Payout journals in the ledger

> A payout moves a shop's money from its own ledger account into `PAYOUT_CLEARING`, then into `PAYOUTS_SENT` on success or back to the shop on failure, using journal ids that retries cannot duplicate.

_Part of [Weekly seller payouts](weekly-seller-payouts.md)_

Every payout is a set of ledger journals tied to one [`Payout`](weekly-seller-payouts.md) row. When the weekly job picks a shop, it posts a journal that takes the full balance out of the shop account and parks it in the holding account `PAYOUT_CLEARING`. The journal id is simply the payout id, and this happens in the same transaction that inserts the [`Payout`](weekly-seller-payouts.md) row. Later the send job asks Stripe to move the money. If Stripe accepts, the money moves from `PAYOUT_CLEARING` to `PAYOUTS_SENT` (a platform account that totals what has left). If Stripe definitely refuses, the same amount moves from `PAYOUT_CLEARING` back to the shop account as a reversal. Either follow-up only posts if the payout row was still `PENDING` and the update changed it. Retries must never post the same journal twice. So the follow-up ids are made by [Deterministic journal id for the follow-up step of a payout](derive-journal-id.md), which turns the payout id plus a step name into the same UUID every time. The week itself is chosen by [Monday of the week, in UTC, as a date string](monday-of.md), so a re-run in the same week hits the unique shop and week key. The posting itself is done by [the ledger service](recording-money-in-ledger.md).

**Look at:** [`PayoutJobs` in payout.jobs.ts](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/payments/infra/payout.jobs.ts#L33) · [`deriveJournalId` in payout.jobs.ts](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/payments/infra/payout.jobs.ts#L98) · [`mondayOf` in payout.jobs.ts](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/payments/infra/payout.jobs.ts#L51)

## Pieces

- [Deterministic journal id for the follow-up step of a payout](derive-journal-id.md): [`deriveJournalId`](weekly-seller-payouts.md) makes a UUIDv5 from the payout id and a step name (`sent` or `reversal`) inside a fixed namespace, so the same payout and step always give the same journal id.
- [Monday of the week, in UTC, as a date string](monday-of.md): [`mondayOf`](weekly-seller-payouts.md) returns the ISO week start (Monday) of a date, in UTC, as `YYYY-MM-DD`; it is the week key stored on the payout.
- Holding account for money in flight to a shop: `PAYOUT_CLEARING` (from [`LEDGER_ACCOUNTS`](recording-money-in-ledger.md)) holds the amount between taking it from the shop and knowing whether Stripe accepted it.
- Account that totals money successfully paid out: `PAYOUTS_SENT` is a local constant naming the account that receives the money once Stripe accepts the transfer.

## What it touches

| Kind | Name | How |
|---|---|---|
| database | [`LedgerEntry`](recording-money-in-ledger.md) | Summed per `SHOP_` account to find balances at or above the minimum, and written by the payout, sent and reversal journals. |
| database | [`Payout`](weekly-seller-payouts.md) | Inserted with `ON CONFLICT ("shopId", "periodStart") DO NOTHING`; moved to `PAID` or `FAILED` only from `PENDING`. |
| job | `payouts.send` | Enqueued with key `payout-send:<payoutId>` in the same transaction that posts the first journal. |
| external | `Stripe Connect transfer (via `[`PayoutProvider`](weekly-seller-payouts.md)`)` | Called with the payout id as idempotency key, so a retry cannot pay twice. |

## Also relies on

- [Recording money in the ledger](recording-money-in-ledger.md): Uses `LedgerService.post` to write each balanced journal inside the caller's transaction.
- [Weekly seller payouts](weekly-seller-payouts.md): These journals are the ledger half of the weekly run and send jobs.

## Watch out

- The first journal uses the payout id as its journal id, while the sent and reversal journals use derived UUIDv5 ids, so they never collide.
- [`mondayOf`](weekly-seller-payouts.md) works in UTC, but the cron schedule runs in `Europe/Warsaw` time. The two can disagree near midnight on a Sunday or Monday.
- Only definite failures (`definite` flag or `StripeInvalidRequestError`) reverse the money. Other errors are rethrown so the job retries with the same Stripe idempotency key.
- `PAYOUTS_SENT` is a plain string in this file, while `PAYOUT_CLEARING` comes from [`LEDGER_ACCOUNTS`](recording-money-in-ledger.md).
